title: Training Note: The Relief Window in Employer Benefit Charging Separation-Response Determinations
content:
For new employer-services representatives. When a determination on an employer's separation response grants relief under Employer Benefit Charging, the relief window is the set of posted charges the relief can take in.

**The rule.** The relief window is every charge posted on the claim when no statement of benefit charges has yet been mailed for the position and charges have been posted, the charges listed on the most recently mailed statement when a statement has been mailed and it lists charges, and no charge otherwise.

**Q. What is "every charge posted on the claim"?**
A. All benefit charges posted to the employer's position on that claim, each at its posted amount.

**Q. Which statement is "the most recently mailed statement", and what does it list?**
A. The statement of benefit charges for the position with the latest mailing date. It lists the benefit charges posted in the quarter it covers, each at its posted amount.

**Q. Does an earlier statement still count once a later one has been mailed?**
A. No. Only the most recently mailed statement's charges are in the window.

**Q. When is the window empty?**
A. When no statement has been mailed and no charge has been posted, or when the most recently mailed statement lists no charge.

**Practice set (hypothetical position: $410.00 posted in the third quarter, $395.00 in the fourth).**

| Statements mailed for the position | Relief window |
|---|---|
| None | $805.00 |
| Third-quarter statement only | $410.00 |
| Third- and fourth-quarter statements | $395.00 |
